 Happening Wednesday: FAFSA Fest, Halloween events, meeting on historic bridges, and more
 Evan Bourtis News10NBC 
 --> 
 ROCHESTER, N.Y. — Here’s your guide to what’s happening around the Rochester area on Wednesday. You can see more upcoming events in our  community calendar. 
 FAFSA Fest at East High
 Rochester organizations are continuing to host events to help students and families navigate the federal and state college financial aid process. The next FAFSA Fest event is on Wednesday at East High School. It runs from 3 to 7 p.m.
 This marks the 13th year of FAFSA Fest in Rochester, which is in partnership with schools, the Rochester Education Foundation, and the Rochester College Access Network. Experts will be at these events to help with filling out both the FAFSA and the New York State Tuition Assistance Program (TAP) forms. The series kicked off on Oct. 8 at Hillside Children’s Center. Here are the upcoming events:
 Wednesday, Oct. 28, 3 to 7 p.m. at East High School, 1801 E. Main St.
 Friday, Oct. 30, 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. at REOC, 161 Chestnut St.
 Tuesday, Nov. 3, 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. at Edison High School, 655 Colfax St.
 Wednesday, Nov. 4, 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. at Edison High School, 655 Colfax St.
 Wednesday, Nov. 4, 5 to 7 p.m. at REOC, 161 Chestnut St.
 Monday, Nov. 9, 8:30 to 10 a.m. at Rochester Early College IHS, 85 Adams St.
 Monday, Nov. 9, 2 to 4 p.m. at Rochester Prep HS, 305 Andrews St.
 Tuesday, Nov. 10, 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. at EMHCS, 27 Zimbrich St.
 Tuesday, Nov. 17, 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. at Padilla HS, 95 Norton St.
 Sunday, Nov. 18, 8:30 a.m. to noon at Wilson HS, 501 Genesee St.
 FAFSA applications for the 2027 to 2028 school year opened in late September, marking the program’s earliest launch date in history. You can learn more about applying for FAFSA in this story .
 Halloween events
 Halloween-themed events continue in the Rochester area, including at R-Centers, libraries, and farms. On Wednesday, the Edgerton R-Center on 41 Backus St. is hosting a haunted house experience. It costs $5 per person at the door and runs from 5:30 to 8 p.m. Also, the Charlotte Branch Library on 3557 Lake Avenue is inviting families to come in and to decorate a Halloween mask. It runs from 4 to 5 p.m.
 The Rochester City School District’s Parent Leadership Advisory Council is also hosting a Halloween event on Wednesday. Families can stop by the Henry Hudson School No. 28 on Humboldt Street for trunk-or-treating, activities, and community resources. It runs from 5:30 to 7 p.m. You can learn more about upcoming Halloween-themed events across the Rochester area in this story .
 Early voting continues
 Early voting continues on Wednesday for the general election. The Monroe County Board of Elections says over 37,000 voters have cast ballots since early voting opened on Saturday.
 You can cast your ballot through Sunday, Nov. 1, at early voting sites in your county or on Election Day on Tuesday, Nov. 3. This year, all 435 House seats and 35 of the 100 Senate seats are up for grabs. There are also some key local races and state-level races, including the governor’s race between Gov. Kathy Hochul and Nassau County Executive Bruce Blakeman.
 News10NBC is your election headquarters. You can see our guide to early voting, key races, and candidate pitches in this story . Read the latest on early voting turnout here .
 Meeting on historic Olmstead Canal Bridges
 Monroe County is holding an open house on Wednesday to allow the public to weigh in on the future of three historic pedestrian bridges in Genesee Valley Park.
 This comes ahead of a study that will develop recommendations for the short-term and long-term maintenance of the bridges. The Olmsted Brothers firm built those bridges in the 1910s to reconnect the park’s paths that the Erie Canal severed. The county is looking for feedback from people who use those bridges for walking, running, cycling, or other activities.
 MORE: Historic Olmsted bridges over Erie Canal in Genesee Valley Park need repairs, but who’s responsible? 
 The open house is happening from 5 to 7 p.m. at the Genesee Waterways Center on Elmwood Avenue. There will also be a guided walking tour of the bridges starting at 5 p.m. For more information, click here. 
 First responders memorial dedication
 Local leaders and first responders will gather at the Civic Center Plaza at 11 a.m. on Wednesday to dedicate a first responders’ memorial. The memorial aims to honor Monroe County’s firefighters, EMS professionals, 911 dispatchers, and more.
